cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Iterable Fall Release Adds Native RCS, Nova Conversations, Integrations Hub, and New AI Agents
stories.plain: Iterable's biggest platform update in years bundles agentic AI agents (Nova Intelligence), a native integrations hub, RCS messaging, and a conversational layer into one continuous learning loop. This matters because it collapses the gap between customer data, decisioning, and cross-channel execution inside a single CEP — changing how the platform is bought and evaluated.

stories.head: Dataiku Launches Agent Management to Track and Govern AI Agents Across Any Platform
stories.plain: Dataiku's new Agent Management layer discovers, measures value, and flags risk for AI agents regardless of where they were built. This is a direct answer to the governance gap that enterprises face as agentic deployments multiply — it gives buyers a cross-platform control plane, which shifts what 'enterprise-ready AI' means in procurement conversations.

stories.head: TransUnion's Matt Spiegel: Only 13% of Marketers Have Fully Scaled AI Due to Fragmented Data
stories.plain: TransUnion's EVP explains why confidence in AI outpaces actual readiness: siloed teams, fragmented data, and ROI measured in time saved rather than revenue growth. The AI confidence-readiness paradox is a practical framework for understanding why most marketing AI pilots stall before scale — critical context for anyone buying or building in this space.

stories.head: Klaviyo CMO: Whoever Owns the Customer Record Wins the AI-Mediated Buying Journey
stories.plain: Klaviyo's CMO argues the real competitive battle is over first-party customer data, not content, because AI assistants now sit between brands and buyers. The insight reframes CDP investment as a GEO and brand survival issue — if a model answers instead of your site, your customer record is the last moat you control.

stories.head: B2B Brands Turn to Creator Video to Resist AI-Generated Slop and Boost AI Search Visibility
stories.plain: B2B marketers are investing in creator-led video as a dual strategy: differentiating from AI-generated commodity content and earning citations inside AI search answers. The piece links content authenticity directly to generative engine optimization, making it actionable for anyone planning 2027 content budgets in a world where AI answers replace search pages.

stories.head: OpenAI testing third-party-style tracking in ChatGPT ads
stories.plain: OpenAI is experimenting with a persistent identifier for ad tracking inside ChatGPT, similar to third-party cookies. This matters enormously because it signals how the dominant AI assistant could become a measurable ad channel — while raising fresh consent and privacy questions that will shape how marketers can buy and govern campaigns there.

stories.head: IAB sets new standards for agentic buying and measurement
stories.plain: The IAB has released frameworks standardizing how AI agents handle media proposals and how contracts for advertising measurement should be structured. Industry-wide standards directly shape how martech is bought and governed, so this is a foundational shift for anyone building or procuring agentic ad systems.

stories.head: Marketo co-founder Jon Miller rethinks B2B marketing automation for the AI age with Phave
stories.plain: Jon Miller, who built Marketo, argues legacy marketing automation was never designed for modern B2B buying groups and has launched Phave as a replacement. When the person who defined a category says it is broken and ships something new, it signals a genuine platform shift worth tracking for buyers and builders alike.

stories.head: Iterable Fall Release: native RCS, Nova Conversations, Integrations Hub, and new AI Agents
stories.plain: Iterable's major platform update adds agentic Nova Intelligence Agents, a native Integrations Hub, RCS messaging, and a conversational layer that links every customer interaction into a continuous learning loop. It moves Iterable from a messaging tool toward a full decisioning engine, changing what buyers should expect from a CEP.

stories.head: Dataiku launches Agent Management to track and govern AI agents across platforms
stories.plain: Dataiku's new Agent Management layer discovers all AI agents running across an enterprise, measures their value, and flags risk — regardless of where they were built. As companies deploy more agents, cross-platform agent governance becomes a critical buying criterion, making this a direct answer to a gap most martech stacks currently have.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The rise of AI coworkers inside marketing teams
body: Across the month, vendors stopped pitching AI as a feature and started shipping it as a named team member with a job description. Snappy Kraken's "marketing operations coworker," HubSpot's platform rebuild around agents, and Marketo co-founder Jon Miller's rethink of B2B automation all point to the same structural shift: the unit of deployment is no longer a tool but a role.

For decision-makers this changes the org-design question. You are no longer asking which software to buy; you are asking which human roles get augmented, which get replaced, and who owns accountability when the agent acts autonomously. IAB's new standards for agentic buying signal that the industry is beginning to answer that question with governance, not just enthusiasm.
ev: MarTech Series · Snappy AI coworker launch

themes.head: AI search rewrites the purchase funnel
body: AI assistants are now injecting themselves between brand and buyer at the moment of intent — recommending, filtering, and in some cases actively advising consumers not to purchase. The ecommerce piece and the "AI is telling consumers not to buy your product" piece together describe a funnel where the marketer no longer controls the last mile of discovery.

B2B brands are responding by investing in creator video precisely because human-authored, high-trust content is harder for AI summaries to flatten into generic answers. OpenAI testing third-party-style ad tracking inside ChatGPT shows the other side of the coin: the platforms building these assistants are already monetising the attention they intercept, creating a new paid-search dynamic marketers must learn quickly.
ev: MarTech · AI tells consumers not to buy
MarTech · B2B creator video vs AI slop

themes.head: Proprietary data as the real competitive moat
body: Two pieces this month made the same argument from different angles: AI outputs are only as good as the data fed in, and that data is now the primary differentiator. MarTech's "the real AI advantage is what your company already knows" and TransUnion's Matt Spiegel on the "AI confidence-readiness paradox" both warn that generic models trained on public data will converge, leaving proprietary data as the last defensible edge.

Iterable's "memory" feature — connecting every customer interaction into a persistent record — is the product embodiment of this thesis. Marketers who have not yet audited what first-party signals they actually own, and how clean those signals are, are building AI strategies on borrowed ground.

themes.head: Agentic governance moves from theory to standard
body: The IAB publishing standards for agentic buying and measurement is the clearest signal yet that autonomous AI action in media is no longer a pilot programme — it is a procurement reality that needs rules. Dataiku's agent-management dashboard and MarTech's AI governance framework piece show the same pressure building on the enterprise side: someone must own oversight of agents that spend money and contact customers.

The governance gap is especially acute because agents can now act across platforms simultaneously. The risk is not that AI does the wrong thing; it is that no human knows it did anything at all — which is exactly the problem the IAB standards and internal governance frameworks are designed to close.

themes.head: The CMO's job shrinks to what AI cannot own
body: Klaviyo's Jamie Domenici framed the leadership question bluntly: when the assistant writes the answer, the CMO's remaining value is judgment, taste, ethics, and brand conviction — things that cannot be prompted into existence. Agile Brand's agentic sales piece echoes this, arguing that the manager's job is shifting from directing activity to orchestrating systems that direct themselves.

This is a strategic forcing function, not just a cultural one. Marketing teams that cannot articulate what uniquely human decisions they are making — and why those decisions matter — will find budgets and headcount absorbed by the automation layer. The "do you really need so much marketing?" piece suggests that pressure is already arriving in boardroom conversations.

month.takeaway: Every headline this month is a variation on one underlying shift: AI is collapsing the distance between intent and action across the entire marketing stack, forcing leaders to decide urgently what humans, data, and governance must anchor that system before the agents do it for them.
